lead: SpaceX reads Buy today at +36 on a −100 to +100 scale (Buy line +30), but any call would be capped at Hold by two quality red flags, and it is still building history (day 5 of 10). It moved from Insufficient data on 2 Oct because forecast revisions now have live data, lifting coverage to 74% (70% needed) and bringing the Demand bucket back in.
bullets: A reading is back, but not a call yet. 74% of indicator weight now has live data vs the 70% needed (it was 62% on 2 Oct): forecast revisions (DM2, 8 of 100 points) count again, showing 2027 earnings per share of $1.94 expected today vs $0.64 expected 90 days ago (+203.5%), a big jump from a small base, so treat it with care. Even once confirmed, two quality red flags cap the call at Hold: free cash flow was −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026, and the operating loss was 1.6x the interest bill over the same two quarters.

Demand scores +100, on a thin base. 57% of the Demand weight has live data (the bucket needs 50%). In the June quarter, vs the same quarter a year earlier, Connectivity (Starlink) revenue grew 66%, AI 247% and Space 29%; Google searches for Starlink were 24.4% above the same 4 weeks of 2025 (a noisy measure: the Starship flight fell in that window). Much of the AI jump came from renting out computing capacity, and one AI customer alone was 12.2% of company revenue in the 6 months to June (10-Q).

The price is extreme vs peers. Valuation scores −100: investors pay 114.3x expected profit over the next 12 months vs 31.0x for Iridium, the only space peer with a usable P/E, a one-peer comparison (+269%); SpaceX's 114x is above the 80x range peers must pass, so the page adds a caution, but it still counts as very expensive. On total company value vs operating profit before depreciation it is 372x vs 8.4x for the median of four peers.

Price trend scores +100, helped by a fall in the peers. The price is 18.7% above its average since listing ($144.11) and 32.0 points ahead of the space peers over 63 trading days: the shares are up 14.5% over that time while the peers fell an average of 17.5%. The shares closed at $171.09, +7.63% on the day vs +0.87% for the Nasdaq-100, 19% below their post-listing high close ($211.40 on 16 Jun) and 27% above the $135 IPO price.

Money flows are neutral. Liquidity scores +8, unchanged from 2 Oct: buying vs selling volume is neutral (1.04x up-day vs down-day volume, last 20 trading days), the dollar index is 3.01 points higher than 20 trading days ago, and markets price a 21% chance of a Fed rate rise at the late-October meeting, down from 30% a month earlier (Polymarket). Short interest fell 12.0% vs a month earlier (2.4% of float). Share supply is rising: 656m shares (5.0% of all shares) unlock in October and about 1.3bn (9.9%) just after Q3 results.
defects: Coverage 74% (above the 70% floor); a call is possible once 7 of 10 trading days agree. Forecast revisions (DM2) are live again: the forecast 90 days earlier is now $0.64 a share vs $1.94 today, above the minimum base, though still a small one.
Quality override O3: 2 red flags (free cash flow −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026; operating loss 1.6x interest), so any call is capped at Hold.
VL3 (P/E vs own history) removed: no earnings history yet. To be reinstated when history allows.
Revenue and margin trends (DM1, DM6) blank: too few quarters filed with the SEC.
No company guidance, so DM3 is blank.

Forward P/E vs peers rests on one peer (Iridium): the other seven are loss-making or outside the 2x-80x data-quality range. The 85.6x is Yahoo's figure; price ÷ the FY2027 consensus of $1.89 gives about 79x. SpaceX's own 85.6x and 323x (EV/EBITDA) are above the 80x range that peers must pass, yet are still scored.
Price trend +100 comes from short-history measures and from peers falling further; the shares fell 12.7% over 63 trading days.

Customer concentration and related parties are not scored: one AI customer ('Customer B' in the 10-Q, not named; press reports suggest Anthropic, unconfirmed) was 12.2% of revenue in the 6 months to June, about 19.5% of June-quarter revenue (Unite.AI); another customer was 17.9% across all three segments in the same 6 months. The 10-Q balance sheet shows about $13.3bn of related-party debt at 30 Jun (details in its Note 17, not reviewed here), and Terafab is a joint project with Tesla.
No cash runway line: cash and securities of $100.0bn vs free cash flow of −$25.0bn in 6 months (rough estimate: 6-8 quarters before new funding).
Demand inputs (DM4a/b/c, DM5) are entered by hand from results releases and Google Trends. DM5 (search interest) is a noisy attention measure that jumps on news.
Short interest as % of float (LQ2) and trading volume (LQ1) shift mechanically while lock-ups add tradable shares.

segments.name: Connectivity (Starlink)
segments.sells: Starlink satellite internet: home and business broadband, aviation, maritime, government (Starshield) and direct-to-phone service.
segments.buyers: Consumers (12.0m subscribers in June 2026), airlines, shipping lines, businesses and governments.
pos: The only profitable part: 38.6% segment operating margin in the Jun 2026 quarter (35.7% a year earlier).
Mostly monthly subscriptions, so revenue recurs.
+66% vs the same quarter a year earlier; subscribers doubled to 12.0m.
neg: Share of sales fell from 64% to 55% (Jun 2025 → Jun 2026 quarter) because AI grew faster.

Revenue per subscriber is lower than a year ago: Connectivity revenue grew 66% while subscribers doubled (roughly −17% per subscriber). Management says average revenue per user held at $66 a month vs the March quarter.
Satellites must be replaced every few years, so capital spending never stops.

segments.name: AI (xAI and X)
segments.sells: xAI: Grok chatbot subscriptions and API, advertising on X, and AI computing agreements (renting out data-centre capacity).
segments.buyers: Consumers and businesses (Grok), advertisers (X), and companies buying AI computing.
pos: +247% vs the same quarter a year earlier; now 33% of sales (18% a year earlier).
New AI computing agreements made the segment EBITDA-positive in the Jun 2026 quarter ($1.1bn adjusted EBITDA; $1.6bn of computing revenue).
neg: Still loses money: segment operating margin −49% in the Jun 2026 quarter (−207% a year earlier).
Takes most of the capital spending: $15.8bn of the $18.4bn capex in the Jun 2026 quarter (86%) was for AI, and management expects a similar level in each of the next two quarters.
Advertising on X is shrinking: $367m vs $426m in the same quarter a year earlier.
Much of the jump came from new computing agreements, and one customer (not named) was 12.2% of company revenue in the 6 months to June; how repeatable these deals are is not yet known.

segments.name: Space
segments.sells: Falcon and Starship launches, Dragon crew and cargo flights, and development work for NASA and defence.
segments.buyers: NASA, the US Space Force and other agencies, commercial satellite operators; it also launches SpaceX's own Starlink satellites.
pos: +29% vs the same quarter a year earlier.
Owning the launcher lets SpaceX put up its own Starlink satellites at cost, which rivals cannot match.
neg: Loss-making while Starship is developed: operating loss $542m in the Jun 2026 quarter (segment margin −56%).
One-off missions, not recurring: revenue swings with launch timing ($619m in the Mar 2026 quarter vs $962m in June).
Smallest part: 12% of sales in the Jun 2026 quarter.
The shift in mix alone took 30.5 pts off segment operating margin vs a year earlier (latest quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier, each part's margin held at that earlier level).
Recurring revenue share down 8.7 pts in a year to 55% of sales (latest quarter).
Fastest-growing part (AI (xAI and X), +247% vs a year earlier) earns below the company segment operating margin.
Concentration: Connectivity (Starlink) is 55% of sales (latest quarter).

shift.title: What the shift means for SpaceX
pos: Faster growth: revenue +92% vs the same quarter a year earlier (Jun 2026), led by AI (+247%).

Losses narrowed sharply in the June quarter: all segments together earned −1.8% operating margin vs −23.8% a year earlier, helped by the AI computing deals. But the March quarter was −41.4%, and over the half year losses widened: −16.7% (6 months to Jun 2026) vs −11.6% a year earlier.
neg: Less recurring: subscription-based Connectivity fell from 64% to 55% of sales while AI, which relies on newer and less proven deals, rose from 18% to 33%.

2026-10-05.lead: SpaceX reads Buy today at +36 on a −100 to +100 scale (Buy line +30), but any call would be capped at Hold by two quality red flags, and it is still building history (day 5 of 10). It moved from Insufficient data on 2 Oct because forecast revisions now have live data, lifting coverage to 74% (70% needed) and bringing the Demand bucket back in.
bullets: A reading is back, but not a call yet. 74% of indicator weight now has live data vs the 70% needed (it was 62% on 2 Oct): forecast revisions (DM2, 8 of 100 points) count again, showing 2027 earnings per share of $1.94 expected today vs $0.64 expected 90 days ago (+203.5%), a big jump from a small base, so treat it with care. Even once confirmed, two quality red flags cap the call at Hold: free cash flow was −$25.0bn in the 6 months to Jun 2026, and the operating loss was 1.6x the interest bill over the same two quarters.

Demand scores +100, on a thin base. 57% of the Demand weight has live data (the bucket needs 50%). In the June quarter, vs the same quarter a year earlier, Connectivity (Starlink) revenue grew 66%, AI 247% and Space 29%; Google searches for Starlink were 24.4% above the same 4 weeks of 2025 (a noisy measure: the Starship flight fell in that window). Much of the AI jump came from renting out computing capacity, and one AI customer alone was 12.2% of company revenue in the 6 months to June (10-Q).

The price is extreme vs peers. Valuation scores −100: investors pay 114.3x expected profit over the next 12 months vs 31.0x for Iridium, the only space peer with a usable P/E, a one-peer comparison (+269%); SpaceX's 114x is above the 80x range peers must pass, so the page adds a caution, but it still counts as very expensive. On total company value vs operating profit before depreciation it is 372x vs 8.4x for the median of four peers.

Price trend scores +100, helped by a fall in the peers. The price is 18.7% above its average since listing ($144.11) and 32.0 points ahead of the space peers over 63 trading days: the shares are up 14.5% over that time while the peers fell an average of 17.5%. The shares closed at $171.09, +7.63% on the day vs +0.87% for the Nasdaq-100, 19% below their post-listing high close ($211.40 on 16 Jun) and 27% above the $135 IPO price.

Money flows are neutral. Liquidity scores +8, unchanged from 2 Oct: buying vs selling volume is neutral (1.04x up-day vs down-day volume, last 20 trading days), the dollar index is 3.01 points higher than 20 trading days ago, and markets price a 21% chance of a Fed rate rise at the late-October meeting, down from 30% a month earlier (Polymarket). Short interest fell 12.0% vs a month earlier (2.4% of float). Share supply is rising: 656m shares (5.0% of all shares) unlock in October and about 1.3bn (9.9%) just after Q3 results.
